title: Christ's Sacrifice and the Eucharist
english: Having been offered once to bear the sins of many, he will appear a second time apart from sin. And again: 'He did not commit sin, and there was no deceit in his mouth'; and behold, he offers himself for us; indeed, he did not offer himself for himself, but for the people.

While he says, 'He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood will live through me, just as I live through the Father who sent me' (John 6:54-56), what then do you eat, heretic: the divinity or the humanity? For Christ did not say, 'He who eats my divinity,' but, 'the flesh' (John 6:51).
I myself receive by faith the flesh of the life-giving Word which gives life; therefore the Savior said, 'Those who eat from this bread will never taste death for eternity' (John 6:51); those who…
translator_notes: The text begins and ends mid-sentence, indicated by ellipses.
The phrase 'the flesh of the life-giving Word which gives life' reflects the Greek 'τῆς τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ Λόγου ζωοποιοῦσαν σάρκα'.
baehrens: PG 76; CPG 5228 (Dialogus cum Nestorio) dial rem close
